title: Unmeasurable Backgrounds
context: Text over gradients, images, and overlays
whyItMatters: Complex or changing backgrounds can make a single contrast measurement unreliable, so the text needs a stable visual boundary.
learningObjectives: Understand why tools can report indeterminate results for images.
Apply protective overlays to support text visibility.
Recognize risks from changing background content.
lessonParagraphs: Contrast is easier to evaluate when text sits on a solid color. A photograph, video, or gradient contains many changing colors, so a tool can report an indeterminate result instead of guessing.
A measurement at one point does not guarantee that the rest of a word is readable. A bright area in an image can sit behind some letters, and a dynamic image can change after it has been checked.
A scrim is a semi-transparent dark overlay between an image and text. It can darken bright areas and provide a more stable background for light text.
Solid blocks behind text or a shadow that creates a boundary are other options. The goal is a resilient container that protects legibility over a complex background.
keyTakeaways: Complex photographs can vary too much for one local measurement to represent every letter.
Dynamic backgrounds can change and reduce legibility.
Scrims or solid blocks can protect the text boundary.
reviewFlags: The document says Avene reports indeterminate for these backgrounds. Confirm this matches current product behavior before displaying it as a product fact.
internalNote: The research also mentions drop shadows and the lightest or darkest pixel behind text.
